label: rem:lagrange-resolvents
title: Lagrange resolvents and spectral form
html:
Let \zeta=e^{2\pi i/n}. The discrete Fourier transform on C_n (Lagrange resolvent transform) diagonalises the cyclic action: \sigma(w_k) = \zeta^{-k} w_k. Any C_n-invariant polynomial constraint on the coordinates x_j transforms to constraints on C_n-equivariant combinations of the Fourier modes w_k.

For n = 5 (Bring's surface), the three power-sum equations become:

\begin{align}
  w_0 &= 0
    &&\text{(linear projection),}
    \\[4pt]
  w_1w_4+w_2w_3 &= 0
    &&\text{(Hermitian quadric),}
    \\[4pt]
  w_1^2w_3+w_4^2w_2+w_2^2w_1+w_3^2w_4 &= 0
    &&\text{(symmetric cubic).}
    
\end{align}

The quadric pairs conjugate modes (w_k with w_{5-k}). The cubic pairs squared modes in the skip-one pattern. These are the C_5-equivariant invariants h_2 and h_3 (aggregate color quantities).
